title: Token Line-Item Orbit: role-aware cost builder & CSV export UX
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a compact, role-sensitive token-level cost analytics canvas ("Orbit") that surfaces line-item cost breakdowns, attribution, and an export builder for CSVs and billing feeds. The component must scale from 10s to 100k line-items via progressive disclosure, support role-scoped views (engineer, finance, product), and provide a pricing-pattern preview (rate bands, SKU mapping) before export.
objective: Create a reusable Console UX pattern for token-level cost clarity: fast scanning of hot cost contributors, accurate attribution across prompts/conversations, and an export composer that maps to customer billing schemas.
scope: Design end-to-end flow: main Orbit table (compact/expanded rows), sparklines for token delta, attribution badges, row actions (pin, annotate, convert-to-slab), export builder modal (column mapping, grouping, rate-band preview), and contextual tips for non-financial users.
acceptance_criteria: Compact Orbit table shows: model, route, prompt fingerprint, tokens, cost, sparkline delta, top attribution tag
Expanded row reveals token-level slices and KV-cache hits + sample prompt fragments for audit
Role toggle (Engineer|Product|Finance) reorders columns and exposes role-specific helpers
Export builder allows column selection, custom tag mappings, and a rate-band preview that estimates exported totals
Prototype loads large datasets in <2s using progressive row virtualization patterns
Design reviewed and accepted by PM (Luis Ortega) and Eng owner (Priya Nair)
design_notes: Use an orbital visual motif: central summary row with expandable lanes radiating attribution contexts
Compact-first by default to keep Console density high; inline sparklines sized to 20px height
Favor readable microcopy for pricing fields; show both unit-cost and billable-cost where quantization applied
Export builder must show a small sample (first 10 rows) with transformed columns before confirm
Provide CSV templates for common schemas (billing-ledger, chargeback, finance-import) with one-click presets
feedback: PM Luis Ortega: Like the role presets; ask to add a 'Compliance' preset that includes request IDs and audit columns
Eng Priya Nair: Concern about rendering 100k rows; suggests server-side pre-aggregation and pagination for the expanded slices
Design review (Sofia Patel): Suggests stronger affordance for pinned rows and a way to surface why a row is expensive (cost tree)
UX Research (Ben Holt): Early sessions show finance users prefer explicit 'billable vs invoiced' columns rather than inferred labels
decisions: Ship compact table + lazy-expanded slices to avoid client memory spikes
Add compliance preset to export builder as requested by PM
Include a lightweight cost tree visual in the expanded drawer rather than full graph to keep layout compact
Prototype will include a 'rate-band preview' that runs the customer's current pricing slab against the sample rows
tradeoffs: Live sparklines vs server-rendered thumbnails: chose client SVG sparklines for better interactivity at the cost of some CPU on large pages
Full export preview of entire dataset would be expensive; we limit preview to first 100 rows and sampling heuristics
Showing raw prompts raises privacy concerns; show redacted prompt fragments by default with opt-in full text for permitted roles
